title: One Nanoscale Zn(II)-Nd(III) Complex With Schiff Base Ligand: NIR Luminescent Sensing of Anions and Nitro Explosives

material_class.structural_family: centrosymmetric Zn2Nd4 Schiff-base nanocluster with co-crystallized zinc chloride methanolate

synthesis.procedure: Zn(OAc)2·2H2O (0.30 mmol, 0.0658 g), NdCl3·6H2O (0.60 mmol, 0.2154 g), and H2L (0.30 mmol, 0.0324 g) were dissolved in 50 mL MeOH at room temperature, then 1.0 mol/L triethylamine in EtOH (1 mL) was added. The mixture was stirred and heated under reflux for 30 min and filtered. Yellow crystals of 1 formed by slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the filtrate at room temperature after 1 month, were collected by filtration, and dried at 120 °C for 2 h. In the crystalline solid, [ZnCl2(H2O)CH3OH] coexists with the Zn2Nd4 complex.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature dissolution; reflux during reaction; room-temperature crystallization; 120 °C drying
synthesis.time: reflux 30 min; crystallization 1 month; drying 2 h
synthesis.vessel_or_method: reflux then slow diethyl ether diffusion into the filtrate
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered after reflux; yellow crystals obtained by slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the filtrate at room temperature after 1 month; collected by filtration and dried at 120 °C for 2 h

properties.summary: The Zn2Nd4 cluster shows ligand-sensitized NIR Nd(III) emission (most intense line at 1054 nm) in CH3CN, with τ = 6.2 μs and Φem = 0.8%. NIR luminescence is quenched by anions and nitro explosives, most sensitively by H2PO2− (KSV = 4.67 × 10^5 M−1) and TNP (KSV = 1.46 × 10^5 M−1); lifetimes drop to 4.1 and 5.2 μs with 1.8 μM H2PO2− and 5.6 μM TNP, respectively, consistent with mainly dynamic quenching.
